title: A generic projective closed subscheme has a unique flat DVR closure
statement: Let $R$ be any discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-field], let $n\geq0$, and let $E\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_R$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-kun-projective, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $Z_K\subset E_K=E\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}K$ be any closed subscheme [def-pc-fibre-product]. There exists a unique closed subscheme $Z_R\subset E$ flat and finitely presented over $R$ whose restriction is $Z_K$ as a closed subscheme of $E_K$ [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. On every affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}C\subset E$, if $J_K\subset C\otimes_RK$ is the ideal of $Z_K$ on that chart, the ideal of $Z_R$ is the inverse image $J=\{c\in C:c\otimes1\in J_K\}$; this description commutes with localization of $C$ and specifies the gluing on overlaps. The quotient $C/J$ is $R$-torsion-free (multiplication by each nonzero scalar of $R$ is injective) and flat. Every geometric fibre of $Z_R$ has the same Hilbert polynomial, for the given embedding, as $Z_K$ [def-sfb-projective-fibre-hilbert-polynomial]. The empty closed subscheme is included. No flatness of $E/R$, excellence of $R$, or finite-type hypothesis on a map from $\operatorname{Spec}R$ to any other base is required.

source.place: Lemma 3.7 and its contraction-of-the-kernel proof, printed pp.264--265, specialized to the structure-sheaf quotient on a closed projective subscheme; constancy of the Hilbert polynomial as used in Theorem 3.2. Archival PDF WANTED; primary PDF read online.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and let $g:Z_K\to E$ be the given immersion followed by the generic-fibre projection. For every affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}C\subset E$, its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}(C_K/J_K)$, where $C_K=(R\setminus\{0\})^{-1}C=C\otimes_R K$, by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] and the affine description of a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This proves that $g$ is quasi-compact: inverse images of affine opens are affine and hence quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. It is quasi-separated as well: over each such $U$, its diagonal is induced by the surjective multiplication map $(C_K/J_K)\otimes_C(C_K/J_K)\to C_K/J_K$, and is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]; hence the diagonal is a closed immersion globally and [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated] applies. The structure sheaf of $Z_K$ is quasi-coherent (locally it is the sheaf associated to the coordinate ring). Thus [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] makes $g_*\mathcal O_{Z_K}$ quasi-coherent, and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel] makes $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_E\to g_*\mathcal O_{Z_K})$ quasi-coherent. Its sections are ideals, since they are kernels of ring maps. On $U$ they are exactly $J=\ker(C\to C_K/J_K)$, the asserted inverse image.

source.place: Tag 01LC (lemma-pushforward-quasi-coherent); Tag 01LB (kernels of quasi-coherent modules); Grothendieck Bourbaki 221 Lemma 3.7 kernel construction

proof.text: Here is the localization calculation, including possible torsion in $C$. For any multiplicative subset $T\subset C$, the ideal of the restricted generic subscheme is $T^{-1}J_K$. A fraction $c/t\in T^{-1}C$ maps into this ideal precisely when some $u\in T$ satisfies $uc/1\in J_K$, equivalently $uc\in J$. Thus its contraction is $T^{-1}J$. In particular this holds for principal opens and for stalks. On overlaps both restrictions of $\mathcal J$ are therefore the same kernel sheaf, with the identity identifications satisfying the cocycle condition. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme] to $\mathcal J$: it gives a closed subscheme $Z_R\subset E$ with affine rings $C/J$. After inverting the nonzero elements of $R$, the ideal generated by $J$ is $J_K$: every element of $J_K$ is $c/r$ with $r\ne0$, and then $c/1=r(c/r)\in J_K$, so $c\in J$. Consequently $(C/J)\otimes_RK=C_K/J_K$, compatibly with all the restriction maps just computed. This identifies the restriction of $Z_R$ with $Z_K$ as a closed subscheme, rather than merely up to an abstract isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01IN (lemma-closed-subspace-scheme); elementary fraction membership calculation for the kernel in Bourbaki 221 Lemma 3.7

proof.text: The kernel definition gives an injective $R$-linear map $C/J\to C_K/J_K$. The target is a $K$-vector space, so multiplication by every nonzero $r\in R$ is invertible there. Therefore $r\bar c=0$ in $C/J$ implies $\bar c=0$. By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $R$ is a principal ideal domain; [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] now makes every $C/J$ flat over $R$. By [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-local-criterion], each stalk of an affine quotient chart is flat over the corresponding base local ring. The charts cover $Z_R$, so the stalk definition [def-weil-flat-morphism] gives scheme flatness; this also agrees with [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. Hence $Z_R\to S$ is flat.

source.place: Tag 0AUW (lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat), part (1), PID case; morphisms.tex Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize)

proof.text: The given embedding makes $E\to S$ projective [def-kun-projective], hence proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]. Its closed subscheme $Z_R$ is proper over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. In particular it is separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], thus quasi-compact, and it is quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. The composite $Z_R\hookrightarrow E\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_R$ is a closed immersion: the composite identifies the underlying space with a closed subset, and on a standard affine chart its ring map is the composite of the two quotient surjections, so [def-weil-closed-immersion] applies. It is the embedding used below.

source.place: Tags 01WC (lemma-projective-proper), 01W5 (lemma-closed-immersion-proper); schemes.tex Tag 01QO affine closed-immersion criterion

proof.text: Every ideal of $R$ is principal [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], hence finitely generated; this is the Noetherian condition [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Since $Z_R\to S$ is of finite type, $Z_R$ has an affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}B_a$ with each $B_a$ a finite type $R$-algebra [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation], each such algebra is finitely presented over $R$. This is local finite presentation of $Z_R\to S$. Its quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness were established in step 4; together these give finite presentation as specified in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Only Noetherianity of the DVR itself has been used.

For uniqueness, let $Y\subset E$ be any flat closed subscheme with the prescribed generic restriction, and on $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ let its ideal be $I$. Then $B=C/I$ is flat over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], applied to the affine open $Y\cap U$. Since $R$ is a domain, [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain] implies that $B$ is $R$-torsion-free. Thus $B\to B\otimes_RK$ is injective: a class mapping to zero is killed by a nonzero denominator from $R$, hence is zero. The generic restriction says that the kernel of $C_K\to B\otimes_RK$ is $J_K$. Taking its inverse image in $C$ and using the injection gives $I=\ker(C\to B\otimes_RK)=J$. Therefore the ideal sheaves of $Y$ and $Z_R$ agree on every affine open, so they define the same closed subscheme [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf, def-weil-closed-immersion]. This even proves uniqueness without imposing finite presentation on the competitor.

source.place: Tag 0538 (lemma-flat-torsion-free); elementary denominator criterion in Bourbaki 221 Lemma 3.7 uniqueness

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-projective-hilbert-polynomial-locality] to the embedding of step 4 and the flat finitely presented morphism established in steps 3 and 5. It gives a locally constant geometric fibre polynomial $P_s$, unchanged by every field extension. The spectrum of the domain $R$ is irreducible: its generic point $(0)$ belongs to every nonempty basic open. Hence every nonempty open contains the generic point, so a locally constant function takes its generic value everywhere (intersect its constancy neighbourhood with the generic point). Thus every geometric fibre polynomial is the generic one. The field-extension clause of the cited node identifies that polynomial with the Hilbert polynomial of $Z_K$ over $K$ for the given embedding [def-sfb-projective-fibre-hilbert-polynomial]. If $Z_K$ is empty, then $J_K=C_K$ and $J=C$ on every chart, so the constructed scheme is empty and its polynomial is zero, as also covered by the cited node. At no step was the map $C\to C_K$ assumed injective; only the quotient $C/J$ embeds. No excellence or external finite-type base hypothesis occurs.

Read the item, the report and all 24 cited node statements in full. The item statement and stmt_deps match clones/live and side-live byte for byte; both still show it as unsplit, so nothing supersedes this delivery. It is a first split with no new nodes; proof_deps = union of the step uses, and there is no cycle. The archival Bourbaki 221 L3.7 PDF is not in literature/, so I checked the mathematics directly and against Stacks 0538/0539/0AUW (more-algebra.tex 4913-4954). S1: the inverse image of affine Spec C is Spec(C_K/J_K); g is affine, hence separated, hence qs; 01LC pushforward plus the qcoh kernel gives J = ker(C -> C_K/J_K). S2: contraction commutes with T^{-1} (checked from fraction equality) and J.C_K = J_K, so the restriction equals Z_K as an ideal. S3: C/J injects into a K-space, so it is torsion-free, hence flat over the PID; the 00HT stalk node gives scheme flatness. S4: projective => proper, closed => proper, separated => qs; the composite embedding is elementary. S5: DVR Noetherian plus 00FP gives lfp, and with S4 qcqs this is finite presentation. S6: competitor B = C/I is flat, hence torsion-free (domain), so B -> B_K is injective and I = J. S7: the locality node's hypotheses are met; Spec R is irreducible, so the polynomial is constant; the base-change clause plus the def node's geometric-extension sentence identify it with Z_K's; the empty case is covered. Small cases: P^0_R; Z_K empty; vertical E = V(pi x1) with torsion in C; nonreduced V(x1^2); the point [1:1/pi], where the affine chart is K but the projective closure meets the special fibre. Duplicate search (flat/scheme-theoretic closure, DVR+flat+generic fibre) finds only the special case lem-trf-nodal-generic-component-closure. Batch 5: lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain is a Mathlib commutative-algebra leaf, and the path through lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space is the Proj Sym = base-change P^n identification (01NF/01O3); neither is part of the trace formula or Poincare duality, so both are accepted. All 12 declared generic tool_uses are accepted. No SGA citation.
